summary: Batched route starvation during tapered autoscaler recovery causing sustained p99 throughput regression
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (VectorMaps Inc.) observed a sustained p99 throughput regression on their dedicated reserved pool starting 2026-03-10 14:30 UTC. The degradation aligns with an autoscaler shrink followed by a tapered recovery window where short-lived high-concurrency streams repeatedly acquired and held GPU slots during warmup, preventing normal batched routes from filling and causing long tail queuing. Impact:
- Customer reported 3x increase in request latency p95->p99 and 40-60% drop in throughput for batched text-generation routes.
- Affects production traffic for multiple routes; some traffic fell back to hosted fallback model variants causing higher cost and inconsistent outputs.
Environment:
- Dedicated pool: reserved-capacity-vecmaps-usw (8x A10g equiv GPUs)
- Region: us-west
- Time window: 2026-03-10 14:30 UTC onwards
- Routes: /v1/generate-batched, /v1/stream-chat (batched backends), customer uses pinned model opt-13b for priority routes
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a mix of long-lived batched generation requests and a burst of short 1-2 token short-stream connections at high concurrency (50-100 concurrent short streams).
2) Ensure autoscaler min_replicas at low baseline (2 GPUs) and cooldown window set to default 300s so autoscaler aggressively shrinks after observed drop in average load.
3) During the autoscaler recovery window, observe GPU attach logs and batcher fill rates for batched routes.
4) Measure p95/p99 for batched route and correlated slot allocation timelines from allocator telemetry.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:29:52Z allocator: shrink_to=2 triggered by 60s low load metric
2026-03-10T14:30:15Z serving-runtime: attach_request id=txn-8f1d short_stream=true duration=0.8s hold_slots=1
2026-03-10T14:33:00Z metrics: route=/v1/generate-batched p95=320ms p99=2.4s throughput=45req/s baseline=120req/s
comments: Priya Nair (Support): Initial triage - customer seeing repeated short streams during autoscaler recovery. Asking SRE to pull allocator traces and prefetch lease state for pool reserved-capacity-vecmaps-usw.

Luis Ortega (SRE): Assigned - gathering allocator, batcher and prefetcher traces. Hypothesis: short warmup streams are obtaining prefetch leases that persist for lease_ttl, blocking slot reuse and starving batchers while autoscaler is in cooldown.

Customer (VectorMaps Eng - Jamie): We started a new feature at 14:25 that spins many short model-check requests. Rolling that back reduced error rate briefly but p99 stayed elevated until autoscaler spun back up.

Luis Ortega (SRE): Correlated with autoscaler shrink at 14:29. We see lease_ttl defaults of 120s; short streams are sequentially reusing same pattern, keeping slots occupied and preventing batch fill. Recommending temporary change: increase autoscaler min_replicas to 4 or disable prefetch for short routes as workaround.
Priya Nair (Support): Noted workaround suggested to customer; requested approval to patch customer's routing policy to reduce prefetch aggressiveness while we investigate.
Luis Ortega (SRE): Added linked investigation to allocator heartbeat (INT-330?) and noted potential follow-up PR for prefetch lease eviction logic.
investigation_notes: 01 - Correlation: Autoscaler shrink at 14:29 reduced active GPUs. Immediately following, short warmup streams (mean duration 0.7s) repeatedly acquired prefetch leases (TTL 120s) and occupied slot objects, preventing batched requests from filling target batch sizes.
02 - Batcher telemetry shows sustained low fill-rate (30-40%) for batched routes while short streams maintained steady attach churn; combined with fewer GPUs caused throughput to fall ~55%.

03 - Allocator traces show slot objects moved to 'pinned' state tied to prefetch lease; lease release did not occur promptly on short stream completion when autoscaler was in recovery (race between prefetcher and allocator release path).

04 - Hypothesis: Prefetch lease release path depends on heartbeat from warmup sidecar; during autoscaler recovery sidecar restart sequence introduced a window where leases weren't reclaimed promptly. Also TTL expiry was long enough to allow multiple short streams to hold onto slots sequentially.

05 - Secondary factor: default autoscaler cooldown prevented new GPUs from being added until recovery window elapsed (300s), so even when workload ramped the platform was slow to re-provision capacity.
06 - No signs of driver-level GPU errors; this appears scheduling/allocator-level resource contention rather than hardware faults.
07 - Related tickets: SUP-712909 (deferred-warmup-causing-spotty-gpu-assignments), SUP-371400 (allocator-heartbeat-skew) - useful traces and prior mitigation notes.
resolution:
Workaround applied (customer consented):
- Increased pool min_replicas from 2 -> 4 for reserved-capacity-vecmaps-usw to reduce chance of slot starvation during recovery window.
- Temporarily disabled aggressive prefetching for short-stream route (/v1/stream-chat) for the customer via routing override.
- Customer rolled back the short-model-check feature burst.
Post-mitigation observations: latency/p99 recovered to baseline within ~6 minutes of changes and autoscaler stabilized.
Next steps (tracking):
- Engineering task created to add lease-release-on-shortstream-termination and to reduce default prefetch TTL for short streams (PR referenced below).
- Consider autoscaler cooldown tuning: expose per-pool cooldown or quick-provision path when significant queueing is detected.
